chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abdallah ibn Sinan who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the interpretation of 'In the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate'. He said: The Ba is the Baha (Splendor) of Allah, the Sin is the Sana (Exaltedness) of Allah, and the Mim is the Majd (Magnificence) of Allah.

key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ: In the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate

ai.seo_question: What is the esoteric interpretation of the letters in the Basmala according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Abdallah ibn Sinan seeks the esoteric meaning of the Basmala from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who interprets the initial letters as abbreviations for divine attributes: Baha (Splendor), Sana (Exaltedness), and Majd (Magnificence). This interpretation highlights the Shia scholarly tradition of viewing the Basmala not merely as an invocation but as a concise theological statement encapsulating the majesty and glory of Allah, reinforcing the spiritual significance of beginning actions with His name.
